extracted.intended_audience: public affairs officers (PAOs), joint force commanders (JFCs), combatant commanders (CCDRs), and military planners
extracted.subtask_description: Doctrine and procedural guidance for Department of Defense public affairs (PA) and strategic communication (SC) activities, including principles, tenets, audience considerations, planning, and roles/responsibilities for producing and releasing information and imagery during joint military operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preeminence of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: First impressions strongly influence perceptions and later judgments; timeliness is a recognized element of news and can determine who frames the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adversaries can communicate false or misleading information faster than the truth; JFCs should be prepared to assume some risk to ensure public communication is timely so accurate and contextual information is available; delay increases the chance that corrective information will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency and Repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recency is a key component of newsworthiness and information retention; repetition improves processing and retention of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information must be delivered in a timely fashion, multiple times, and from multiple sources. Continuous public engagement throughout an operation best supports strategic communication themes and operational objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: News is a cultural narrative shaped by the values and ideology of those producing it; ideology, ethnocentricity, and culture affect how information is presented and perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural impacts on presentation and reception of information; attempts to mitigate negative public opinion after the fact are often ineffective, so cultural considerations should be second nature in planning and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Propaganda is adversary communication—often biased or misleading—designed to influence opinions, emotions, attitudes, or behavior for the sponsor's benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same factors that make news compelling (conflict, violence, oddity) make propaganda effective. Anticipate adversary exploitation and limit potential by preemptive release of information; when preemption is not possible, be prepared to respond rapidly to counter propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs Across the Range of Military Operations
rubrics_metrics.description: PA is inherent in all military activities (engagement, deterrence, crisis response, major operations) and is a key enabler for managing and delivering public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A synchronized and coordinated PA effort with interagency partners facilitates success in other military operations and should be integrated across the full range of operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing Trusted Counsel to Leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: PA core competency: anticipate and advise commanders on the public information implications of operations and prepare leaders to communicate with audiences and media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes analyzing the information environment, monitoring public understanding (domestic and foreign), and providing lessons learned. PAOs should brief and coach commanders for media engagements and public messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing Morale and Readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: PA activities inform military personnel and families about policies, programs, and operations affecting them, thereby reducing uncertainty and stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA should incorporate planning and resources to address family concerns, prepare Service members for media attention (including human-interest coverage), and provide guidance on interviews to mitigate negative impacts on morale and readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fostering Public Trust and Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective PA builds public trust and understanding of the military's role and contributions to national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing accurate, timely, and clear information is critical to sustaining public support for military operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating Global Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ PA in concert with other information capabilities to inform international audiences about US military actions and capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with Department of State, host and partner nations, and allies, and manage releases within OPSEC constraints to enhance allied support and international understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting the Command Strategy (synchronization of actions, images, and words)
rubrics_metrics.description: PA must synchronize actions, images, and words to support command strategy and provide continuous, credible, timely, and accurate information and imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA must be involved in operational planning, have access to open-source reports and relevant intelligence, anticipate adversary propaganda, and be aggressive in getting accurate information out first (even if unfavorable) to maintain credibility and gain the information initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterring Adversaries through Information
rubrics_metrics.description: PA can disseminate information and imagery to convey possible countermeasures and US intentions to deter adversary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly communicate US goals, expectations, why concerns matter, and intended actions if adversary refuses to comply. Counterpropaganda aimed at domestic resolve should be addressed to maintain public trust and influence adversary planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Information shall be made fully and readily available
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD must make timely, accurate information available to the public, Congress, and the news media consistent with statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support FOIA in both letter and spirit; answer requests from organizations and citizens quickly unless release is precluded by national security constraints or valid statutory exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Free flow of information to the Armed Forces
rubrics_metrics.description: A free flow of general and military information shall be made available, without censorship or propaganda, to members of the Armed Forces, civilian employees, contractors, and dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information and programming to internal audiences across available media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Do not withhold information to avoid criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Information will not be classified or otherwise withheld to protect the government from criticism or embarrassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withholding must not be used as a tool to conceal mistakes or prevent scrutiny; transparency promotes credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Withhold only for legitimate security/privacy reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Information shall be withheld only when disclosure would adversely affect national security or threaten safety or privacy of Service members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply legitimate OPSEC and privacy considerations when making release decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Coordinate with other government agencies when required
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD's obligation to inform the public may require coordination with other government agencies to expedite information flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate releases as necessary with OGAs to ensure timely and lawful disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Propaganda has no place in DOD PA programs
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD PA programs must not use propaganda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA activities must be truthful and not intentionally misleading or manipulative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet: Tell the Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: PA personnel will release only accurate information; long-term success depends on integrity and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deception undermines trust. Address unfavorable information openly and honestly as soon as possible; failure to acknowledge leads to speculation and loss of public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet: Provide Timely Information and Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should be prepared to release timely, factual, coordinated, and approved information and imagery about operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and accurate releases can make the release source the media's preferred provider; PAOs must establish expeditious processes for release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet: Practice Security at the Source
rubrics_metrics.description: All DOD personnel and contractors are responsible for safeguarding sensitive information and being aware of OPSEC issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official information and imagery must be approved for release prior to dissemination; personnel should be trained on OPSEC when interviewed or sharing information, including on social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet: Provide Consistent Information at All Levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Information from multiple official DOD sources must be coordinated; conflicting releases jeopardize credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate releases to ensure consistency with DOD and supported commander guidance before public dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet: Tell the DOD Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should designate official spokespersons but educate and encourage personnel to convey appropriate aspects of the DOD story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely, releasable information to personnel so they can project confidence and promote public understanding during interviews or casual conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience: American Public
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders have an obligation to inform the American public about the nation's military to enhance morale, readiness, and public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active engagement demonstrates community partnership and stewardship of national resources; provide information that helps the public understand military roles and missions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience: International Community
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and imagery can be globally available; international audiences may have equal or greater interest in operations, particularly overseas activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with DOS, host and partner nations, and allies; keep international community informed within OPSEC limits to preserve alliances and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience: Internal (command information programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Command information programs communicate with Service members, DOD civilians, contractors, and families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal channels to inform and prepare internal audiences for media interactions and operational impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience: Adversaries
rubrics_metrics.description: PA distributes timely, truthful, and accurate information to adversary audiences to counter misinformation and deter action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronize PA with IO/MISO to ensure coherent messaging toward adversaries given the fluid information environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Strategic Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: SC principles include leadership of the communication process, credibility, dialogue, unity of effort, responsiveness (right audience/message/time/place), understanding, pervasiveness (every action sends a message), results-based orientation, and continuity (analysis, planning, execution, assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these principles to guide integrated efforts (actions/images/words) in support of USG objectives; assessment measures, methods, and resources must be developed and incorporated to inform decisionmaking and adjust operations toward desired end states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate SC into Operational Planning and Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: SC planning must be integrated into military planning (OPLANs/OPORDs) and coordinated with OGAs and multinational partners; messages should support nested themes at all levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document SC in plans, synchronize themes/messages/images/actions with operations, and develop assessment measures to support commanders' decisionmaking and mission accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission of Joint Public Affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan, coordinate, and synchronize US military public information activities and resources to support the commander's intent and concept of operations (CONOPS); advise, execute, and evaluate PA activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs generate information requirements to assess foreign public perceptions and integrate that information into mission planning; PA is to be incorporated into every phase of joint operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA CONOPS: openness, speed, and balanced coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: PA CONOPS should provide open, independent reporting with maximum disclosure and minimum delay and create an environment that encourages balanced coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop well-defined, concise plans and determine the lowest level authority for release to ensure timeliness; incorporate PA activities into each phase of operations while considering OPSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASD(PA) Role: initial source and PA guidance authority
rubrics_metrics.description: ASD(PA) determines who should serve as the initial source of release for joint/multinational operations and delegates PA release authority to appropriate commanders; approves and disseminates PA guidance, plans, and annexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASD(PA) also facilitates deployment of DOD Media Pool, oversees COMCAM employment and distribution, establishes crisis/wartime PA cells, facilitates AFRTS resources, coordinates PA policy across DOD and partner organizations, ensures PA guidance in CJCS orders, and may provide training and media analysis support.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASD(PA) Responsibilities: media support and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversee and facilitate media and visual information capabilities and support for operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes facilitating DOD Media Pool deployment, COMCAM product distribution and follow-on use, establishing crisis PA cells, facilitating AFRTS deployment, and providing periodic training/familiarization to accredited media to support embed programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combatant Commanders: PA planning and support
rubrics_metrics.description: CCDRs must coordinate and synchronize SC capabilities, develop PA annexes to OPLANs/OPORDs, and plan for media and PA support across operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific tasks include planning priority transportation for media and PA personnel, providing PA resources and movement priorities, planning communications assets (internet/satellite/telephones), considering bandwidth/IT requirements, granting media access when feasible, preparing PPAG (PA policy, contingency statements, release authority, declassification guidance, themes/messages/talking points), preparing for DOD Media Pool deployment, establishing media operations centers (MOCs), assisting media access to units and personnel, and planning command information programs and ground rules for release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretaries of Military Departments: organize, train, equip PA forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop PA policies and doctrine, provide resources, organize/train/equip AC/RC PA and VI personnel to conduct PA activities in support of CCDRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure readiness and prompt availability of PA resources, provide predeployment tailored training, conduct Service-specific PA programs in support of joint and multinational operations, and consider appropriate security clearance levels for PA/VI personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs: promulgate and oversee PA doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: CJCS promulgates joint PA doctrine and ensures PA annexes to plans/orders comply with published doctrine, policy, and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide PA representation to National Military Command Center cells during crises, support DOD media pool deployment coordination, provide senior officers with communications expertise, and ensure CJCS orders contain appropriate PA guidance paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director, Defense Media Activity (DMA) functions
rubrics_metrics.description: DMA provides information products to DOD and external audiences across media, delivers radio/TV programming to Service members and families, and provides joint education and training for PA/VI personnel at DINFOS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DMA consolidates previous service media activities to provide joint media support, programming, and professional development; see appendices and DOD directives for access and further details.
